# All-branch integration — 23 October 2026

The user authorized continuing until all published branches are merged into main. The source inventory in `all-branches-source.json` records all 54 non-main branch heads observed at the start. Integration preserves their ancestry and the current main baseline `a630cdcbabaaf04786d3b068cafdabbe19613b76`.

The current physical-execution and natural-language/planning workstreams combine without code conflicts. Accomplishment, supervised knowledge, organization, delegation and ordinary citizen lifecycle owners are reconciled through the existing resolver, dispatcher, gateway, persistence and session owners. The resolver preserves resource/facility prerequisite entry points when selecting a Job-specific knowledge policy. Delegated effects retain target-time scope checks; lifecycle unavailability remains an immediate direct-authority fence. All stores remain registered, bounded and closed through their existing owners.

The older connected-client branch is superseded by the subsequently qualified main/client implementation. Its history is retained without restoring obsolete workflows, instrument versions or physical owners. Diagnostic/evidence branches are also retained; their archival workflows keep their original restricted triggers. No frozen case, recipe catalog, model, execution allowance or acceptance assertion is relaxed.

The original frozen assessment and its original production baseline remain unchanged. A separate integration workflow records the actual new JAR and complete production inventory at the reviewed commit, then uses the same 45 cases, exact expectations, frame/client identity checks, outcome classifications and conservation evidence. Its measurement collection is not a gameplay-success score gate. A complete measurement report must retain any failure rather than call it successful gameplay.

The six Agent 2 focused workflows also accept this integration branch so genuine interpretation and planning measurements can qualify the combined source. Required source builds, native execution and actual models run in GitHub Actions. Local Python harness validation passes 72 cases; source/native/model qualification is pending until the exact new campaign concludes. No integration PASS or merge is claimed by this preparation record.

The first integrated campaign `bbfe52ec64232265a927c135280a24eb3e547057` recorded 123 core test failures. One confirmed cause is a shared registration capacity conflict: 17 explicit save readers exceed the old 16-entry table. The trusted reader table now has a finite 32-entry bound. Reader version sets, the 16 migration-rule bound, migration storage/time/record budgets and execution limits retain their existing values. Integration tests exercise all 17 owners, unknown/future-version rejection, duplicate domains and the 32-entry boundary. The original failed campaign remains evidence, not acceptance.

The retained XML also exposes the older mandate codec's seven-action ceiling after the typed Effect alphabet grew to eight with placement. The constructor and codec now derive their finite action-set bound from that alphabet. Stored rights remain explicit sets: existing seven-action grants do not acquire PLACE, unknown action names still fail enum parsing, and child scopes still require exact subsets. Worker/resource/container/area, duration, cumulative budgets, current authority and revocation rules retain their existing checks.

The corrected owner suite at `d95b5ab56a3bfb611fa4064fbaf2dcface44fbf4` executes 2,028 core cases; 2,026 pass and two assertions retain pre-integration totals. The organization reader test now recognizes the explicitly implemented citizen schema-1-to-2 migration while retaining its no-organization-migration check. The generic registration boundary test still verifies exact N acceptance and N+1 refusal using the new finite table limit. Frozen gameplay/model cases and expected outputs are unchanged.

The final documentation integration records exact source campaign identities, failures and fixes, merge commits, original history and independently executed local audit results. Documentation GitHub Actions remain excluded. The live branch inventory is checked again at completion so a branch that moves during qualification cannot be silently counted as integrated.

### Acquisition evidence across delivery families

Combined native checks exposed that IMP-022 reconciled only crop acquisitions: real resource admissions became `KNOWLEDGE_REQUIRED` on reuse. Acquisition reconciliation now accepts every registered delivery family through the existing `ResourceDelivery` receipt verifier. It validates acknowledged Jobs bindings, enrollment, exact method/run references, full physical lineage, cumulative credit and cross-job receipt reuse before publishing the first shared method revision. Crop accomplishment/teaching evidence keeps its existing scope; personal learners and future method revisions do not inherit access. A focused integration test rejects a successful status with incomplete resource receipts and checks shared use, personal isolation, foreign ownership, exact revision and restart persistence.

### Loaded-only nearest observation domain

The unchanged Needle native fixture exposed a second integration regression: the new typed generic container scan treated every unloaded cell in its bounded envelope as uncertain evidence, unlike the existing loaded-only nearest contract. The Fabric adapter now excludes cells outside the eligible loaded domain for all container types and facilities. Unknown evidence for a loaded object still fails closed; selected objects that unload are rejected by final freshness validation. No chunks are loaded and no fallback to a different object type is added. The original native fixture, quantities and expected bindings are unchanged.

The combined frozen qualification workflow now triggers on production source changes as well as its corpus/instrumentation paths, ensuring later integration fixes receive an exact-head production build and frozen-case run. The original corpus, prompts and expectations remain byte-identical.

### Dependent completion publication fence

The controlled native composition fixture exposed a real publication race: Bootstrap reported an admitted resource method as complete after Jobs committed, while asynchronous knowledge acquisition was still pending. A following composition could permanently fail KNOWLEDGE_REQUIRED. Bootstrap now has an owner-neutral, bounded asynchronous completion publication port after Jobs acknowledgement and before its final public marker. Fabric uses it to publish the exact resource acquisition through the existing access writer. Pending metadata remains PERSISTING; failed or expired acknowledgement preserves spent effects and fails storage without inventing learned access. Late acknowledgement cannot revive a fenced controller. Three focused controller tests cover delayed success, rejection and expiry/late completion. Original composition fixtures and expectations are unchanged. Planning qualification now also triggers on core/Fabric production changes so this final combined code receives the full frozen planning measurement.

### Archive review after subsystem integration

The Task 3 archive reviewer correctly preserved its original historical rule that only two binary classes had changed. That rule cannot describe the combined source, which intentionally includes additional subsystem classes. Its explicit integration mode now requires the successful combined qualification's byte-pinned production JAR, verifies the complete production source inventory and frozen corpus against an ancestor build, and matches the full zero-failure module suite/case inventory in the native archive. Every current client/server/release copy, source identity, frame, physical receipt and all nine native cases remain mandatory. Historical member differences are recorded without claiming unchanged production. The original strict binary-difference mode remains available for its original scope. Nine focused provenance tests cover changed production, changed tests/corpus/binary, unrelated history and retry artifact selection. Failed-job retries select each producer's latest artifact from the same run and exact source head, preserving successful earlier jobs while rejecting older passing artifacts when a later attempt exists. This revision changes verification only; the qualified production remains the ab04fec build.
